statement: A snail crawls 3 cm every minute. How far does it crawl in one hour? Give your answer in metres.

choices.misconception: I thought a metre is 1000 cm, so I divided 180 by 1000.
I thought an hour has 100 minutes, so I got 300 cm, which is 3 m.
I changed 180 cm into metres by dropping just one zero.
I found the distance in centimetres and forgot to change it into metres.

hints: Find the distance in centimetres first, then check the unit.
Work out how many minutes are in one hour and find the distance in centimetres. Then change centimetres into metres using how many centimetres make one metre.
One hour is 60 minutes, so the snail crawls 60 x 3 = 180 cm. 100 cm make 1 m, so 180 cm is 1.8 m.

solutions.reliable: In 60 minutes the snail crawls 60 x 3 = 180 cm. There are 100 cm in a metre, so 180 cm is 1 m and 80 cm, which is 1.8 m. The transferable idea: when a question changes units twice, do one change at a time and re-read the unit asked for at the end.

whyOnTest: It needs two unit changes, minutes to hours and centimetres to metres, and each slip lands on a choice, so checking units is the skill tested.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
